name: Bookings Calendar for WooCommerce
author: moiseh

sections.description:
Bookings Calendar for WooCommerce shows the free and the taken slots of your WooCommerce Bookings products on one calendar, so your customers see what is open at a glance — how many spots are left, what is sold out, when the next free slot is — and book it in a click.

Add it with the Bookings Calendar block, in the editor and in block themes, or with the [wbc-calendar] shortcode.

Attention: this plugin is an add-on for the official WooCommerce Bookings extension. It provides the calendar on your pages, not the booking functionality or the bookable product types.

Premium version ($35 one-time, a year of updates): your customers book straight from the calendar, a list of the upcoming free slots, the price on each slot, and filters by category — see the Premium version.

Free features:

  • A Bookings Calendar block for the editor and block themes, and the [wbc-calendar] shortcode — day, week, month and list views
  • The spots left on each slot (“3 spots left”), and a full slot shown as “Sold out”
  • The calendar opens on the first day with a free slot, and a “Next available” button jumps to the next one
  • On a phone, the calendar shows as a list
  • An information tooltip on each slot: its description and the spots left (a Premium feature until 1.1.0)
  • A fast month view: the slots are kept for a few minutes and worked out again as soon as a booking comes in
  • A click on a slot opens its product with that date and time already chosen
  • Your colours, time format, language, first day of the week and start date; slots that cannot be booked shown greyed out, hidden or as usual

Premium version features:

  • Book from the calendar — a click on a slot opens a booking window with that date and time already chosen: one more click and it is in the cart (view demo)
  • Upcoming slots — the next free slots of your products in a short list, each with a Book button, as the “Upcoming Bookable Slots” block or the [wbc-upcoming] shortcode (view demo)
  • The price on each slot, beside the spots left, and in its tooltip
  • A colour for each product — each product’s slots in a colour of its own (view demo)
  • A calendar widget — the calendar in a sidebar, added as a widget (view demo)
  • Filter by product or category — in the settings, the shortcode and the block
  • A calendar of the taken slots — only the booked slots, for a schedule of what is taken (view demo)
  • Live search — the calendar’s search box narrows the slots as you type, without reloading the page (view demo)
  • WooCommerce Accommodation Bookings — accommodations on the calendar too

Get the PRO version here.
sections.installation:
1. Upload woo-bookings-calendar.zip to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress
  3. It’s done. Now you can go to the Settings to configure what you want
sections.faq:
Does it need WooCommerce Bookings?

Yes. The calendar shows the slots of the products of the official WooCommerce Bookings extension, which makes products bookable and takes the bookings. Without it the calendar stays empty, and the plugin says so in your admin.

Why is my calendar empty?

Check that WooCommerce Bookings is active, that you have at least one published bookable product, and that its availability has free slots in the days shown. The calendar opens on the first day with a free slot, and its “Next available” button jumps to the next one.

Does it work with page caching?

Yes. The page can be cached: the calendar loads its slots from the server when it shows, so a cached page still shows the current slots. Those slots are kept a few minutes (“Keep the calendar slots for this many minutes”, 5 by default) and worked out again as soon as a booking comes in or a bookable product changes.

Can a page show several calendars?

Yes, since 1.2.0 — each Bookings Calendar block or [wbc-calendar] shortcode draws its own, for example one per product with [wbc-calendar product="12"].

The calendar is slow to load. What can I do?

The slots are kept for a few minutes, so only the first visit of a week or a month works them out. When even that is slow, it is usually the month view of products booked in short blocks (minutes or hours), where WooCommerce Bookings works out every block: use longer booking blocks, or open the calendar on the week or the list view (Settings › Calendar view, or the block’s opening view).

What does the Premium version add, and what does it cost?

Booking straight from the calendar (a booking window opens with the clicked slot chosen), the “Upcoming Bookable Slots” block, the price on each slot, filters by category, a colour per product, a calendar widget, a calendar of the taken slots and a live search. It is $35, paid once, with a year of updates and support and a 7-day money-back guarantee — see it here.

Developer hooks

PHP filters (add_filter):

  • wbc_fullcalendar_options — the FullCalendar 6 options (array)
  • wbc_calendar_start_date — the date the calendar opens on (Y-m-d)
  • wbc_event_row — one event before it goes to the calendar ($event, $post, $product, $availables)
  • wbc_build_events_array — all the events of one request ($events, $products, $start, $end)
  • wbc_booking_products_args — the query of the products the calendar lists
  • wbc_bookable_product_types — the product types it lists (default array( 'booking' )) — since 1.0.42
  • wbc_available_colors — the colours of the available slots, one per product ($colors, $product) — since 1.0.42
  • wbc_color_available / wbc_color_unavailable — one product’s colour ($product; return a CSS colour)
  • wbc_calendar_class — the calendar element’s CSS classes
  • wbc_shortcode_html — the calendar’s HTML ($html, and since 1.0.42 the shortcode’s $atts)
  • shortcode_atts_wbc-calendar — WordPress’s own filter of the [wbc-calendar] attributes — since 1.0.42
  • wbc_frontend_vars — the values handed to the calendar script (WBCVARS)
  • wbc_pre_build_events_array — return an array of events to answer a calendar’s request with it, before its free slots are worked out (null, $products, $start, $end) — since 1.2.0
  • wbc_cache_key_fields — the POST fields of the events request that make its cache key (add one a wbc_events_request handler sends) — since 1.2.0
  • wbc_max_request_days — how many days one events request may cover (42) — since 1.2.0

JavaScript events (jQuery, on document):

  • wbc_calendar_options (options, $el) — the FullCalendar options, before the calendar is created: callbacks go here — since 1.0.42
  • wbc_events_request (postData, info) — the AJAX request for the events, before it is sent — since 1.0.42
  • wbc_events_loaded (events, info) — the events the server sent, before they are drawn — since 1.0.42
  • wbc_calendar_loaded ($el, calendar) — the calendar is drawn; it is also window.wbcCalendar
  • wbc_event_click (event, jsEvent), and wbc_event_render (event, $element) on document.body
sections.changelog:
1.2.1

  • Hardened: the Bookings Calendar block’s settings use the block editor’s current field sizes — no deprecation notices in the editor’s console
  • Tested with WordPress 7.2

1.2.0

  • New: several calendars on one page — each block or [wbc-calendar] shortcode draws its own (only the first one did)
  • New: without WooCommerce Bookings the plugin says so — a notice on the plugins page and its settings, and a note over the calendar that only an admin sees (the calendar was just empty)
  • New: the Premium features shown on the settings page and in the block’s sidebar, the Premium version’s price and terms on its tab
  • New: a review request on the plugin’s settings page, two weeks after it is installed (dismissed: never again)
  • Changed: the Premium notice shows on the plugin’s own settings page, and comes back 90 days after it is dismissed
  • Fixed: a product whose availability has “Date range” rules sent the slots of every day of its rules, whatever dates the calendar showed — now only the days shown, inside its minimum and maximum booking dates
  • Fixed: a slot wholly inside a not-bookable range of the availability rules stayed bookable on the calendar, and a range overlapping a slot’s start was not taken out
  • Hardened: the spots left of a product with resources are counted resource by resource — those with a quantity of their own add up, those without share the product’s (it asked for a resource read through a property that no longer exists)
  • Fixed: a click on a slot opens its product with that date and time chosen again — the day goes into the booking form once its date picker is ready, its time slots load and the time is picked (the time slots did not load with WooCommerce Bookings 3.x)
  • Fixed: a product deleted, or of a type no longer known, no longer stops the calendar
  • Hardened: the calendar’s slots request covers six weeks at most (one request could ask for years of slots), its cache key is made of the fields that change its answer (a link’s utm_* or fbclid made a new one each), and the “Next available” answer is kept like the slots and answers at once past six months
  • Hardened: the slots are forgotten when a bookable product changes, not on every product saved (every order’s stock change did)
  • Changed: the plugin’s description, FAQ (WooCommerce Bookings, page caching, several calendars, an empty or slow calendar, the Premium version), “Requires PHP: 7.3” and “Requires Plugins: woocommerce” in its header

1.1.1

  • Tested with WooCommerce 11.3 and WordPress 7.1

1.1.0

  • New: a “Bookings Calendar” block for the editor and block themes — its opening view, products and start date in the block’s sidebar (the [wbc-calendar] shortcode stays)
  • New: the spots left on each slot (“3 spots left”), and a full slot shown greyed out as “Sold out” (Settings: “Show the spots left on each slot”)
  • New: the calendar opens on the first day with a free slot, and a “Next available” button jumps to the next one
  • New: on a phone the calendar shows as a list, as long as its slots (not a box scrolling inside the page), and its toolbar wraps
  • New: the information tooltip on each slot (its description, the spots left — now on by default) is now part of the free plugin
  • New: a faster month view — the slots of a request are kept a few minutes (“Keep the calendar slots for this many minutes”, 5) and worked out again as soon as a booking or a product changes
  • Changed: a tidier settings page — a long setting’s label sits on its own line over its field (it ran to four lines in the label column), and a group with one long label shows all its labels that way
  • Changed: taller hours in the day and week views, so a slot shows its time, its name and its spots left
  • Fixed: the information tooltip has its own box (without the Premium version it showed as bare text)

1.0.42

  • New: developer hooks — the wbc_bookable_product_types and wbc_available_colors filters, the shortcode’s attributes through WordPress’s shortcode_atts_wbc-calendar filter (and passed to wbc_shortcode_html), and the JavaScript events wbc_calendar_options, wbc_events_request and wbc_events_loaded; all listed in the FAQ
  • Fixed: the “Display loading” overlay counted on WooCommerce’s blockUI already being on the page; it is now queued with the calendar (under WooCommerce’s current wc-jquery-blockui handle), and the plugin no longer registers a second copy of it
  • Hardened: the calendar script cleaned up, with no change in what it does — the duplicated retry timers and time-label selectors made one, no deprecated jQuery calls ($.trim, .click(), .ajaxSuccess(), .ready()), no stray globals, and the wait for the booking form’s date picker stops after a minute instead of polling for ever

1.0.41

  • Hardened: WordPress.org Plugin Check warnings — the settings save checks its own nonce too, the read-only requests (the dates a calendar link opens on, the event search, the calendar’s product list, the settings tab) are sanitized and marked as such, the settings script’s global is prefixed (wbc_tab_current), and translations are left to WordPress (no more load_plugin_textdomain())

  • Changed: a cleaner Get PRO tab — the PRO features one per row with a check, a red YouTube “Watch demo” button for each feature video, and the buy button at the top and the bottom
  • Fixed: a settings tab whose name has a space opened empty
  • Changed: a cleaner settings page — the settings in a card, one row each with the label and its field aligned, on/off settings as switches, multiple choices as chips, a setting’s sub-options in a panel under it, and Reset set apart from Save

1.0.38

  • Fixed: on phones the week and day views showed a strip of three hours (06:00–09:00) and hid the bookable slots below it; a narrow calendar is now taller and its time grid opens at the first slot (unless a scrollTime is set through the wbc_fullcalendar_options filter)
